Replay

Browser blob storage

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use the browser store to persist bounded opaque bytes in IndexedDB, such as a profile or encoded save. browser_store.odin provides asynchronous operations. Keep I/O outside simulation steps. An operation has one owner and three phases: Idle, Pending, Complete. Submission returning true means work started; only Complete with error None is a success receipt. Close each operation after consuming its result.

Odin
write: storagegd.Browser_Store_Op
if storagegd.browser_store_write(&write, "my-game", "profile", bytes, revision, 4096) {
    // Continue rendering/pumping. Poll on later frames.
}
if storagegd.browser_store_poll(&write) == .Complete {
    if write.error == .None {revision = write.revision}
    storagegd.browser_store_close(&write)
}

Read with browser_store_read. A successful read exposes its revision and browser_store_bytes, which returns owned bytes using the requested allocator. Missing is distinct from an unreadable or corrupt record. Decode and validate application content before installing it. Native calls return Unsupported; the existing staged-file storage functions remain available there.

Writes compare the supplied revision with the stored revision inside one read/write transaction. Revision zero creates an absent key. Success increments the revision; a mismatch returns Conflict without replacing another writer's value. The revision range is 1 through 2^53−1. After a conflict, load the current record and decide how to proceed. The API does not merge profiles or inventories.

Records hold a revision and a Blob. Reads validate shape and Blob size before materializing bytes, then check the copy again on the Godot side. Limits are 1 byte–16 MiB per operation, 16 retained operations and 64 MiB of reserved operation capacity per page. Namespace/key strings use 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, hyphens and slashes. Each namespace maps to an origin-local database named replay/<namespace> with a version-1 blobs store. Namespace separation is organizational; other code on the same origin can access these records.

The writer uses a bounded base64 string because Godot's generic JavaScriptObject method call did not convert PackedByteArray in the tested engine. This incurs temporary encoding/string copies beyond the reserved payload budget. Reads use the JavaScriptBridge buffer conversion. The payload limit is not a total process memory bound.

Success is published from transaction completion, after all requests commit; request success alone is insufficient. Writes request strict durability. These semantics follow the IndexedDB transaction contract. The tested configuration is Chrome on arm64 macOS, including a killed browser after a completion receipt. Browser quota, eviction and user deletion remain applicable; portable power-loss durability is not claimed. Storage errors are surfaced without an automatic volatile fallback.

Closing a pending operation discards its receipt and attempts to abort an active transaction. A write may already have committed. Read its record to determine the result; closing is not proof of rollback. A pending operation does not become successful merely because time has elapsed. A blocked database open reports Open, and a caller may close an operation it no longer wants to await.

tests/replay_browser_store/run.sh exercises the real Godot/WASM bridge and IndexedDB: 1 MiB and 16 MiB exact-content round trips, fresh browser recovery, two tabs writing from the same observed revision, size/corruption rejection, an aborted transaction preserving the old record, and recovery after SIGKILL. It also forces a synchronous request failure followed by completion of the empty transaction; the failed save must remain failed and retain the previous record. The tabs are focused while their Godot loops run; this is stale-tab conflict coverage, not every browser suspension or simultaneous scheduling case.

Scrapyard's profile integration creates its identity before opening the session, saves confirmed preferences and upgrades, and exposes pending/failed saves to the player. A complete run bundle is serialized into one blob by its browser run-save integration. Checkpoint and image dependencies commit together. The separately stored spray preference applies to fresh runs; it cannot silently replace a resumed image.

The JS helper is installed once per page. Reload the page to apply changes to that helper's implementation; operations do not retain pointers into Odin memory.

Cavecrawl's browser checkpoint flow uses the same service for persistent Session identities and token-scoped self-contained archives. It validates ownership and content before resume and retains the initially observed slot revision to reject stale-page replacement.
